note: Three kinds of series are shown here and they are not comparable with one another. The Sensex series is the growth of 100 units invested at the 1979 base, chained from published calendar year returns, so it is an index path rather than a table of year end closes. Gold is an annual reference price per 10 grams of 24 carat metal. Silver is an annual reference price per kilogram. Index points and metal prices measure different things and should be read separately. Missing years are left blank rather than estimated, and 2026 is excluded throughout because the calendar year is incomplete.

series.name: BSE Sensex, growth of 100 from 1979
series.source: Calendar-year Sensex returns as published in the BSE returns series; growth path computed from those returns

series.name: Gold, annual reference price
series.base: Annual reference price, not a year-end close
series.source: Widely published Indian annual gold reference series, 1964 to 2024, as compiled by MMTC-PAMP and reproduced by several Indian financial publishers. 2006 is absent from the published series and is left blank rather than estimated. 2025 is omitted because published sources disagree materially.

series.name: Silver, annual reference price
series.base: Annual reference price, not a year-end close
series.source: Widely published Indian annual silver reference series, 1981 to 2025. 2026 is excluded because the calendar year is incomplete.

events.label: Oil shock and inflation
events.note: Gold nearly doubled in a year as global inflation surged.

events.label: The Hunt brothers and the silver spike
events.note: Global silver was driven to extraordinary levels and then collapsed, the sharpest episode in the metal's modern history.

events.label: Black Monday
events.note: Global equity markets fell sharply in October. Sensex ended the year down 15.7 percent.

events.label: Balance of payments crisis and liberalisation
events.note: Reserves fell to a few weeks of cover. The economy opened, and the Sensex rose 82.1 percent.

events.label: Securities scam
events.note: Diverted bank funds unwound. The year still closed up 37 percent after a violent first quarter and collapse.

events.label: Asian financial crisis
events.note: Currency and banking stress across east and southeast Asia.

events.label: Dot com unwind
events.note: Technology valuations corrected worldwide. Sensex fell 20.6 percent.

events.label: Market crisis
events.note: Concentrated leveraged positions unwound. Sensex fell 17.9 percent.

events.label: Global financial crisis
events.note: The worst year on record for the index, down 52.4 percent.

events.label: Recovery
events.note: The strongest year in the modern series, up 81 percent.

events.label: European debt stress
events.note: Sovereign debt concerns weighed on markets. Sensex fell 24.6 percent.

events.label: Silver doubles
events.note: Silver rose 108.8 percent in a single year on inflation fears and investment demand, then fell for four consecutive years.

events.label: Taper tantrum
events.note: Signals of reduced US stimulus pulled capital from emerging markets.

events.label: Taper and the gold correction
events.note: Global gold fell sharply as the dollar strengthened. The rupee price fell less, cushioned by currency weakness.

events.label: Global sell off
events.note: Growth concerns in China and commodity weakness. Sensex fell 5 percent.

events.label: Demonetisation
events.note: High value notes withdrawn at short notice. The year closed up 1.9 percent.

events.label: NBFC liquidity crisis
events.note: A large infrastructure lender defaulted, tightening credit broadly.

events.label: Covid crash and recovery
events.note: March fell 23.1 percent, the worst month in the series. The year still closed up 15.8 percent.

events.label: Covid and the metals
events.note: Silver rose 56.2 percent and gold reached fresh highs as uncertainty spread.

events.label: Inflation and rate shock
events.note: Central banks raised rates rapidly. Sensex held on, up 4.4 percent.

events.label: The silver repricing
events.note: Silver rose about 120 percent in the year as industrial demand from solar and electronics met constrained supply.
